summary: Join our GIS for Traffic and Highway Engineering training course. Gain essential skills to optimize traffic management and enhance roadway safety.
lede: GIS for traffic and highway engineering uses spatial analysis to turn roadway data into maps and engineering evidence. It is for traffic and highway engineers, transport planners, and GIS analysts assessing corridors and infrastructure priorities. Learners practise integrating traffic counts, applying linear referencing and network analysis, and creating crash and corridor maps with repeatable data-quality and reporting workflows.
audienceIntro: GIS for traffic and highway engineering training suits professionals who manage, analyze, design, or communicate roadway and transport evidence. It supports foundation-to-intermediate learners who need practical GIS workflows rather than advanced software development.
modules: Spatial Analysis for Safety and Operations
Integration and Highway GIS Action Plan
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Basic exposure to traffic engineering, highway planning, transport operations, surveying, or infrastructure asset management. You should be comfortable working with spreadsheets and reading simple maps. No programming experience is required. Advanced GIS automation, Python scripting, enterprise database administration, and production-grade web GIS deployment are introduced conceptually or operationally rather than taught at engineering implementation depth. Bring a laptop capable of running QGIS or access to an ArcGIS Pro environment.
